title: How k changes with temperature
caption: For a reaction with Ea = 50 kJ mol⁻¹, the Arrhenius equation predicts k nearly doubles for each 10 K rise near room temperature (×1.91 from 300 to 310 K) and rises ever faster.
alt: k relative to its value at 300 K against temperature from 290 to 360 K, rising in an accelerating curve; at 310 K it is about 1.9.

checks.name: k rises by a factor of about 1.9 from 300 to 310 K (Ea = 50 kJ mol⁻¹)
